clue.text: Hot air's circulating to plug musical release

indicators.note: a plug sits inside an opening, so this group is pushed into the middle of the show's name

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: things circulating move round, so these letters travel into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
air's read as the word airs

explanation.surface: Blowing off steam turns out to be just the thing for an emotional release through music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot air' reads as one phrase meaning empty talk, but hot is split off as a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the purging of pent-up emotion, a release of feeling, as Aristotle described tragedy providing.

clue.text: Muppet CEO Kermit soon replaced

indicators.note: letters that are replaced are put back in different positions, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: all thirteen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Kermit, boss of the Muppets, is about to be ousted as chief executive.
explanation.walkthrough: Kermit the Frog looks like the answer's subject, but his name is merely raw material for another Muppet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookie Monster is the blue biscuit-loving puppet from Sesame Street, one of the Muppet family of characters.

clue.text: After tango, snubbed stranger's left in lurch

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the shortened word for stranger
a snub nose is short, so the word is cut short by losing its last letter
After puts the rest of the wordplay behind the opening letter

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
stranger means more odd
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone is abandoned in difficulty after a dance with a stranger who then cold-shoulders them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left in the lurch' is the idiom the surface leans on, but lurch alone is the definition, an unsteady movement.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk unsteadily like an infant, so the gait is a kind of lurch.

clue.text: Some irritating sound in my earhole? That does it!

definitions.note: the subject is the irritating noise, and 'does it' stands for the verb

indicators.note: what arrives in the earhole is heard rather than read, so the answer is how a phrase is pronounced

parts.note: an irritating sound is a noise; 'some' supplies the A

explanation.surface: A grumpy listener snaps at a racket blaring into their ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That does it!' reads as an exclamation of lost patience; cryptically, an irritating noise is what does the annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise that grates irritates the hearer; 'does it' refers back to that irritating, which is the verb meaning vexes.

clue.text: Character who looms large in a seminar's novel reading?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for size among the letters that follow
novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken letter for letter
reading is one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A class discussing a novel's dominant character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looms large' reads as a fixed idiom, but 'looms' belongs to the definition and 'large' is wordplay. Note too that 'novel' is the anagram signal, not just the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Silas Marner, the title character of George Eliot's novel, is a linen weaver, someone working at looms.

clue.text: Beset by problems, I lob my soup over some art

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards
something beset by these words is surrounded by them, so the answer sits within the run of letters

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of problems to the start of soup

explanation.surface: A protester throws soup over a painting, as climate activists did in galleries.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls activists throwing soup at Van Gogh's Sunflowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbolism was a late nineteenth-century movement in painting and poetry, so it names a kind of art.

clue.text: Fronts for thieving racketeers announce massive price hike

indicators.note: the front of each word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

parts.note: initials of the five words

explanation.surface: Criminals running a racket declare an enormous price rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price hike' is a natural phrase, but 'hike' stands alone as the definition: a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring walk, the same as a hike over the hills.

clue.text: North African vessel sits in Arno now and then

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
sits as in is situated, so is

indicators.note: now and then means only occasionally, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A boat from North Africa is moored on the River Arno from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arno is the river through Florence and Pisa. The setter later admitted the clue was slightly off; this parse reads sits as IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tunisian is a person from Tunisia, the country on the North African coast.

clue.text: Rock in more expansive bit of space always losing velocity

indicators.note: always losing means each of the two words drops the letter every time

parts.note: more vast
a void is an empty space
v is the physics symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A rock somewhere out in the wider reaches of space is forever slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: The V comes off both VASTER and VOID, which is why the clue says 'always'.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a lump of rock orbiting the Sun, a minor planet.

clue.text: Showing off, dropping name in front of male model

indicators.note: in front of places the shortened word before the final letter
something dropped is let go, so one letter is removed from the word for showing off

parts.note: parading is flaunting oneself
N is the abbreviation for name
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A male model flaunts himself on the catwalk without giving his name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male model' looks like a catwalk figure, but male is a single letter and model alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a pattern or typical example, which is what a model is in the abstract sense.

clue.text: Perhaps seventh word in a limerick's too long for it

indicators.note: the stretch of words is longer than the solution, which therefore lies within it

parts.note: the run from the second letter of word to the first letter of limerick

explanation.surface: A limerick's seventh word has too many syllables to scan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that seventh is just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventh is an ordinal number, the kind that gives position in a sequence rather than quantity.

clue.text: See 1
Christmas visitor possibly taking other end of weighty decoration

indicators.note: taking the other end means one end letter is swapped for the opposite end of another word

parts.note: relatives by marriage visit at Christmas
the other end from its W

explanation.surface: A seasonal guest, perhaps Santa, brings along a heavy ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: The W of INLAW is the first letter of weighty, so it is replaced by weighty's other end, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlay is ornamental material set into a surface, such as wood or ivory work, a form of decoration.

clue.text: Lad very embarrassed to admit papa's promised money

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a son
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
so as in very much
red-faced with shame

explanation.surface: A blushing boy owns up to his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promised money' fits sponsored in the sense of a sponsored walk, where backers pledge cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor someone is to pledge funds for their effort, as charity backers do for a fun run.

clue.text: Making a certain sound when stealing away

parts.note: as meaning at the time that
pirating is stealing, taking for oneself

explanation.surface: Someone makes a noise while sneaking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stealing away' suggests creeping off quietly; here it means taking unlawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirating means pronouncing with an audible breath, the h sound, so it is making a particular sound.

clue.text: One text contains just over a hundred mistakes

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the number goes into the joined words

parts.note: sole means one and only
CI is 101 in Roman numerals
SMS is a text message

explanation.surface: A single document has a little over a hundred errors.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals are a crossword staple: a hundred is C, and adding I makes 101, just over.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette, so solecisms are mistakes.

clue.text: Submariner beginning to navigate through twisted ocean plants

indicators.note: passing through something means being inside it
twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ocean is a sea

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which follows the sailor's name

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel
its initial letter

explanation.surface: A submarine crew steers through twisting ocean weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ocean plants' suggests sea anemones, but those are animals; plants alone defines the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are flowering plants of the buttercup family, also called windflowers.

clue.text: One got on … or came down?

definitions.note: used as in 'came down to', a total

parts.note: a means one
got on a horse

explanation.surface: A rider either climbed aboard or got off again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came down' looks like dismounting, the opposite of getting on, but means came down to, as in a total.
explanation.definitionFit: If a bill came down to ten pounds it amounted to ten pounds: both phrases mean totalled.

clue.text: Massage on vacation limited personal crisis

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside letters go and only the ends stay

parts.note: the first and last letters
Ltd is the abbreviation for limited company
own as in one's own, personal

explanation.surface: A holiday massage that ran short leaves someone in a personal crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal crisis' reads as one phrase, but personal is wordplay and crisis alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A meltdown is a sudden collapse or emotional breakdown, a crisis.

clue.text: Old men up for dancing with yours truly, Methuselah?

indicators.note: letters out for dancing move about, giving a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter
yours truly is a jocular way of saying me

explanation.surface: The ancient Methuselah gets old men on their feet for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is this puzzle's setter, so the name is a pseudonym; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A nom de plume is a pen name, and Methuselah is the pen name this crossword setter writes under.

clue.text: During goalless game, reduced team's rolling with punches

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a nil-nil scoreline, written 0-0

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a football team of eleven reduced by one
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A football side down to ten in a scoreless match is reeling from blows.
explanation.walkthrough: A red card reduces an eleven-player team to ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-two is a pair of quick punches, a left jab followed by a right cross.

clue.text: Semi-retired US prison boss given notice

indicators.note: retiring means going back, and semi says only half of the word does so

parts.note: an American prison governor is a warden

explanation.surface: An American prison governor easing into retirement is handed his notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half, DEN, turns round to NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be warned is to have been told in advance, which is to have been given notice.

clue.text: See 4
Masculine decoration catching zip has gotta hurt

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the word for nothing goes inside

parts.note: has gotta means has to
zip means nothing, zero
to hurt is to ache

explanation.surface: Getting a man's ornament stuck in a zip is bound to hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip' suggests a trouser fastener, but in American slang it means nothing, zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is facial hair grown on a man's upper lip, ornamental in the setter's playful phrasing.

clue.text: Relaxed, or wound up, blowing top

indicators.note: blowing off the top in a down clue removes the first letter

parts.note: wound up as in provoked, mocked

explanation.surface: Someone is either calm or tense and about to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' suggests losing one's temper, but it means beheading the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, so it is a synonym of relaxed.

clue.text: Lioness grabs tail of unlucky antelope

indicators.note: grabbing holds something inside, so one letter goes into the name

parts.note: Nala is the lioness in The Lion King

indicators.note: the tail is the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A lioness seizes an unfortunate antelope's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Y goes in the middle of NALA.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: Tory leader fills political address with extremely nebulous ideas

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so the letter sits within the address

parts.note: No 10 Downing Street, written with I and O for one and nought

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: its opening letter

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so just first and last are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: The Conservative leader packs his Downing Street speech with vague ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Political address' sounds like a speech, but it is the Prime Minister's home, No 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions are ideas or beliefs, often vague ones.

clue.text: Observe silicon and another element at work

parts.note: Si is the chemical symbol for silicon
tin is a chemical element
on as in operating, working

explanation.surface: A chemist examines silicon reacting with a second element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observe' looks like a lab instruction but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit in on a meeting or class is to attend it as an observer without taking part.

clue.text: Country torn asunder without old monarch

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
without means lacking, so the monarch's letters are removed

parts.note: taken letter for letter
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A nation is ripped apart once its former king is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II, hence 'old monarch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa, bordering Egypt.

clue.text: Token of affection almost returned, but interrupted by fish and chips?

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing inserted in its middle
returned means sent back, so the letters run backwards
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a red rose is a romantic gift
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A love token is nearly sent back over a fish-and-chip supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish and chips' looks like one dish; fish is wordplay and chips alone is the definition, with the question mark marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are often ordered as a side dish alongside a main course, an accompaniment.
